chapter_name: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
learning_objective: 🎯 Analyze the serious environmental and social challenges caused by rapid urbanization, pollution, and unchecked development in India.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The addition of contaminants into the natural environment. Includes Water pollution (industrial waste in rivers), Air pollution (smog, vehicle emissions), Noise pollution, and Land pollution.
Cities generate massive amounts of solid waste. Improper disposal leads to toxic landfills, soil contamination, and health hazards like typhoid and cholera.
People flock to cities for jobs (pull factor) and to escape rural poverty (push factor). This creates extreme pressure on urban infrastructure, housing, and water supply.

Unplanned, overcrowded, and dilapidated settlements without basic amenities (like Dharavi in Mumbai). They result from rapid migration and lack of affordable housing. Slum dwellers face severe health and economic risks.
The decline in the productive capacity of land due to over-irrigation (salinity), deforestation, overgrazing, and excessive use of chemical fertilizers.

fun_activity.title: 🔍 Trash Detective
fun_activity.instructions: Look inside your family's dustbin. How much of it is biodegradable (food peels) vs. non-biodegradable (plastic wrappers)? Discuss one way to reduce the plastic waste your household generates!

exam_tips: 📌 Differentiate between point source pollution (a specific factory pipe) and non-point source pollution (agricultural runoff).
📌 Prepare a short note on Dharavi as a case study for the problems of slums and urban planning.
📌 Be ready to suggest practical solutions for urban solid waste management (reduce, reuse, recycle, compost).
quick_recap: ⭐ Air pollution is directly linked to respiratory and cardiovascular diseases.
⭐ Namami Gange is a flagship program by the government to clean and protect the river Ganga.
⭐ The push factors of rural poverty are much stronger drivers of migration in India than the pull factors of urban jobs.
